source_text:
Τοὺς γῆν Αἴγυπτον φεύγοντας δι' ἐρήμου ὁδηγεῖ ὁδόν· οἶδε γὰρ ἡ
σπάνις παιδαγωγεῖν πρὸς ἐγκράτειαν καὶ ἀρχομένους τῆς ἀρετῆς. Προσσκήνωσον τῇ Αἰλείμ πυλῶνες δὲ αὐτοὶ ἑρμηνεύονται, τῆς ἐπὶ τὴν ἀρετὴν εἰσόδου φερούσης σύμβολον καὶ δεῖξον τοὺς ἑβδομήκοντα φοίνικας. Σκήνωσον δὲ κατὰ τὰς δώδεκα πήγας–δεῖ γὰρ καὶ τὰ τῆς νίκης σε ὑποφωνεῖν φοίνικες σύμβολον καὶ τὴν τῶν παθῶν παραμυθεῖσθαι φλόγα παρέχοντα νάματα δαψιλῶς– ἕως ἂν πάντα καθελόντες τὰ ἀλλότρια ἔθνη φθάσωσιν εἰς τὴν γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ἐν ᾗ τὸν μακάριον τῆς ἀπαθείας βιώσονται βίον μισθὸν τῶν πόνων τὴν ἀληθινὴν κομιζόμενοι εὐφροσύνην. 1
thought_title: The desert journey to Elim as the path to freedom from passions
orientation: Evagrius is closing his treatise by comparing the monastic community's progress under its leader to Israel's journey through the desert toward the promised land.
pass_a_gloss: Those fleeing the land of Egypt he guides through the desert on a road; for scarcity knows how to train toward self-control even those beginning in virtue. Encamp at Elim—and the gates themselves are interpreted as a symbol of the entrance leading to virtue—and show the seventy palm trees. And encamp by the twelve springs—for it is necessary both that the palm trees, a symbol of victory, whisper victory to you and that they comfort the flame of the passions by providing streams abundantly—until, having destroyed all the foreign nations, they arrive at the promised land, in which they will live the blessed life of freedom from passions, receiving true joy as the reward for their labors.

choices.why: The verb is a direct imperative addressed to the leader, continuing the instructional voice of the treatise; 'encamp' preserves the military-journey register of Israel's desert march.
The noun denotes lack or want, and the context is ascetic training; 'scarcity' keeps the concrete desert condition rather than an abstract virtue.
The verb means to lead or guide as a tutor; 'train' fits the ascetic context of forming beginners in virtue, avoiding the narrower 'educate'.
The verb suggests a low or subtle utterance; 'whisper victory' conveys the quiet encouragement the palm trees as victory symbols give, matching the gentle guidance theme.
The verb means to soothe or console; the springs comfort the flame of the passions, and 'comfort' preserves the therapeutic register used earlier in the treatise.
The aorist subjunctive with ἕως ἄν expresses the goal of the journey; 'arrive' captures the sense of reaching the promised land after the conquest.

bible_refs.note: ἦλθον εἰς Αἰλείμ, καὶ ἦσαν ἐκεῖ δώδεκα πηγαὶ ὑδάτων καὶ ἑβδομήκοντα στελέχη φοινίκων

pass_b_english: Guide those who are fleeing the land of Egypt through the desert, for scarcity knows how to train people in self-control, even those who are just beginning in virtue. Encamp at Elim—its gates are interpreted as a symbol of the entrance that leads to virtue—and point out the seventy palm trees. Encamp also by the twelve springs, for the palm trees must proclaim victory to you as a symbol, and the springs must cool the flame of the passions by providing streams abundantly. Do this until they have destroyed all the foreign nations and arrive at the promised land, where they will live the blessed life of freedom from passions, receiving true joy as the reward for their labors.
notes: The source has Προσσκήνωσον with a doubled sigma, likely a scribal variant or error for προσκήνωσον; glossed as 'encamp'.
The source has Αἰλείμ for Elim, matching the LXX spelling Αἰλείμ; the brief maps this to 'Elim'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary maps 'Ailim' to 'Elim'; English uses 'Elim'. Correct per names mapping.
last_rejected.ruling: No error; English 'Elim' correctly renders Αἰλείμ per stated glossary mapping.

last_rejected.why: Greek says 'its gates are interpreted/translate as', not 'its gates are interpreted as a symbol'. The 'symbol' comes from σύμβολον later in the clause.
last_rejected.fix: its gates are interpreted as a symbol of the entrance
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly conveys πυλῶνες ἑρμηνεύονται with σύμβολον; 'as a symbol' captures the clause meaning.

last_rejected.quote: the palm trees must whisper victory to you as a symbol
last_rejected.source_quote: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ τὰ τῆς νίκης σε ὑποφωνεῖν φοίνικες σύμβολον
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'for the palm trees must whisper to you of victory as a symbol', not 'whisper victory to you as a symbol'. τῆς νίκης is genitive ('of victory'), not accusative.
last_rejected.fix: for the palm trees must whisper to you of victory as a symbol
last_rejected.ruling: 'Whisper victory to you as a symbol' adequately renders ὑποφωνεῖν τῆς νίκης σύμβολον; genitive sense preserved.

last_rejected.quote: Do this until they have destroyed
last_rejected.source_quote: ἕως ἂν πάντα καθελόντες τὰ ἀλλότρια ἔθνη φθάσωσιν
last_rejected.why: English 'Do this' adds an imperative not in Greek, which continues participial construction from prior imperatives. The subject of φθάσωσιν is 'they' (the disciples), but 'Do this until' makes it seem like the leader is to do the destroying.
last_rejected.fix: until they have destroyed all the foreign nations and arrive
last_rejected.ruling: 'Do this until' naturally continues prior imperatives; 'they' correctly renders φθάσωσιν subject without implying leader destroys.

problems.quote: the palm trees must whisper victory to you as a symbol
problems.why: Palm trees do not whisper; mixed metaphor with springs 'comforting flame'.

problems.quote: comfort the flame of the passions
problems.why: Context suggests quenching/extinguishing, not comforting passions.

problems.quote: Encamp at Elim—its gates are interpreted as a symbol
problems.why: Exodus 15:27 mentions no gates at Elim; gates are imported allegory.
problems.fix: Note: allegorical addition, not biblical text.

problems.quote: for forgiveness shames the sensible person no less than a warning does
problems.why: 'Warning' and 'eternal punishment' may both render the same concept of admonition; reader may miss the link.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or clarify that punishment is the content of the warning.

edits.old: the palm trees must whisper victory to you as a symbol
edits.new: the palm trees must proclaim victory to you as a symbol

edits.old: comfort the flame of the passions
edits.new: cool the flame of the passions

fixed: The gates at Elim are an allegorical addition in the source, not a biblical citation; the English correctly renders the source's allegory.
The glossary issue about 'warning' and 'eternal punishment' does not appear in this passage.
